subject: removing several rows from data frame by unique conditions

messages.author: 20a4c389c493c963
messages.subject: removing several rows from data frame by unique conditions
parts:
I have a data frame with with ~22K rows, with 15 columns. Each row within the DF has its own coordinates, under "lat" and "lon" columns. 
There is another DF of 600 rows with similar "lat" "lon" coordinates that also exist somewhere in the large data set. 

How do I remove the 600 rows based on their unique combination of $lat and $lon without looking them up one by one and removing them manually. 

Ideally, I'd like to say something like any $lan & &lon in DF that exactly match a $lat & $lon that appear in DF2 - remove it from DF. 


Help would be greatly appreciated, 

Renanel

messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] removing several rows from data frame by unique conditions
parts: Also worth noting that the latest Rstudio version supports autocompletion with %>%
On Sunday, March 1, 2015, Yoni Sidi <yon...@gmail.com> wrote:

library(dplyr)
df=data.frame(lat=rnorm(1000),lon=rnorm(1000),a=sample(letters,1000,replace = T))
df1=df%>%select(lat,lon)%>%sample_n(100)
df_new=anti_join(df,df1,by = c("lat","lon"))
df_new%>%nrow
[1] 900
